subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI VISUAL/EDITOR compose handoff now, and what trigger plus temp-file/process privacy guardrails should govern it?
rationale: The feature is coherent and still missing, but it adds local process execution and prompt-file persistence, so automation should not choose the UX or security boundary on its own.

options.title: Approve Bounded Core Flow
options.body: Implement a chosen shortcut or slash command that suspends the TUI, round-trips the draft through VISUAL then EDITOR, never auto-submits, documents privacy/error behavior, and adds focused tests.

options.title: Require Design First
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers settle shortcut conflicts, slash-command discoverability, temp-file lifetime, cleanup, and privacy wording.

options.title: Defer Editor Handoff
options.body: Decline the local editor process launch for now and leave long-prompt ergonomics to inline multiline, vi-mode, or web composer improvements.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement a chosen shortcut or slash command that suspends the TUI, round-trips the draft through VISUAL then EDITOR, never auto-submits, documents privacy/error behavior, and adds focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from the prior issue review and TUI editor/controller history.
